message.content:
**Order placed and filled:** Buy 25 shares of COST at a limit of $905.00 (filled at $905.00, ~$22,625 total; quote at time of decision was $904.13 with a $904.11/$904.15 bid-ask).

**Mandate checks:** COST is on the permitted list; buy-only; order value $22,625 < $25,000 per-order cap; $22,625 < $50,000 daily cap (no other trades today); limit $905.00 is 0.1% above the current market price, i.e., close to market; funded entirely from existing $50,000 cash, so no money leaves the account.

**Summary:** I read Costco's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-01) and checked the live quote ($904.13) and the account ($50,000 cash, 50 GOOGL shares, no COST). The filing shows a business that grew steadily with high-quality cash generation: net sales of $254,453 million (up 5.0% from $242,290 million), operating income of $9,285 million (up 14.4% from $8,114 million), net income of $7,367 million (up 17.1% from $6,292 million), diluted EPS of $16.56 (up from $14.16), and operating cash flow of $11,339 million. Operating margin improved to ~3.65% and net margin to ~2.9%, with the company stating liquidity is sufficient for at least the next twelve months and no unusual legal or control issues disclosed — a consistent, membership-model retailer with rising earnings. At $904.13 the shares trade at roughly 54.6× fiscal 2024 diluted EPS, which is a rich multiple, so rather than take a full position I sized the order at 25 shares (~$22.6k, 45% of cash and under the $25k per-order limit) with a market-close limit of $905.00, which executed at $905.00. The key figures I relied on — revenue $254,453M, operating income $9,285M, net income $7,367M, diluted EPS $16.56, and operating cash flow $11,339M — are recorded in the order's key_figures. I made no other trades, leaving $27,375 of cash and the remaining $27,375 of today's $50,000 budget unused.
